sections.title: Letter sound
paragraphs: The letter (quê) /ke/ has two sounds. Its main sound is the cluster /kw/, heard in the word (quatro) /ˈkwa.tɾu/, which means four.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the sound /kw/, the back of your tongue presses against the soft roof of your mouth. Stop the air, release it, and round your lips quickly into a narrow circle. For the sound /k/, keep your lips neutral while the back of your tongue releases the stopped air. Hold your hand to your throat to feel that your voice is off.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Before the letters a or o, say the sound /kw/, as in the word (quase) /ˈkwa.zɨ/. Before the letters e or i, write this letter as a digraph with a silent letter u. Then say only the sound /k/, as in the word (que) /kɨ/, and in the word (aqui) /ɐˈki/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not add a w sound when this letter stands before the letters e or i. Say the simple sound /k/ as in kite, never as in quick. Also avoid puffing air out when you make this stop. Portuguese plosive sounds are not aspirated, so release the air cleanly.
